task_card.title: Object Stamp Flow - extract an object from one image, place it into another

next_action.description: Wire the Flow. FIRST resolve MPI-607's stale Gate-2 claim (state/files/055e76ab-... and f3f2a8a8-..., heartbeats 2026-08-23, days past the 120-minute timeout) which covers every wiring file. Then the FlowDef in flowsRegistry.js + the op in its 4 files per docs/playbooks/add-flow/01-descriptor-and-ops.md, and convert graph-bench-auto.json / graph-bench-manual.json to the raw editor format. TWO THINGS THE SPLIT DECIDED that the FlowDef must honour: declare the `cutout` step (role image2) BEFORE the `place` step (role image1), because _deriveRunMedia walks steps in declaration order and `place` stamps whatever sits in sourceRole at that moment; and `place` takes mediaRole: 'image2'. Run /mpi-add-flow - it enforces the playbook.

key_decisions: THE SPLIT SHIPPED AS DESIGNED for the CANVAS, and with ONE approved departure at DISPATCH. The drift note said composePlacedObject should keep rebuilding from its own value alone, reading the cutout masks out of that step's value - which would copy both base64 mask layers into `place`'s snapshot too, two copies that can disagree. Fabio approved the alternative before the work started: the masks stay in the ONE step that owns them, and _deriveRunMedia hands `place` the object as the run will see it (the cutout step's derived file when that step did anything, the user's upload when it did not). plan.md § Plan Drift carries the full note.
STEP ORDER IS NOW LOAD-BEARING, and it is the easiest way to break this flow silently. Declare `cutout` before `place` or stage 3 stamps the UNCUT object and everything still runs.

`place` in MANUAL derives NOTHING. The clean object it wants is already image2, put there by the cutout stage, so Manual contributes only the region rect through STEP_PARAMS. Auto derives the stamped composite into image2 via mediaRole.

Stage 2 is skippable BY CONSTRUCTION, no flag: untouched, composeCutObject returns null, the frame reads a null as 'this kind changed nothing', and image2 reaches the run exactly as supplied. Measured on a mounted component, not just the adapter - it also reports NOTHING on mount, and Reset returns it to skipping.

TWO MASK LAYERS, NEVER FLATTENED, and composeObjectAlpha runs against the ORIGINAL RGB so Restore reveals real pixels. That function now lives in MpiStepCutout and is imported by MpiStepPlace, so the preview and the dispatch cannot disagree.

mask_expand_pixels is an INT input, so law 8's 30% must be driven off MpiMaskSquareBbox.size through an MpiMath rather than hard-coded.
